albums.lineage: The latest chapter for a songwriter who stays close to the Cosmic American Music revival this lane tracks, sounding indebted to '70s Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris records.

albums.label: Fire Records
albums.description: Davis's debut draws on pristine Laurel Canyon songwriting from the '60s and '70s and dresses it in gentle country phrasing, all warm harmonies and unhurried tempos. It reads as a straight continuation of the soft-rock/country-rock lineage this lane traces back to.
albums.lineage: A newer voice working directly in the Laurel Canyon/country-rock tradition that feeds this lane, closer to '70s soft rock than jam-band twang.

albums.label: Jealous Butcher Records
albums.description: Samuels' songs sit somewhere between wry confessional folk and loose country rock, working through coming-of-age memory with a deadpan, conversational delivery. It's plainspoken songwriting in the Drag City tradition dressed in warmer, twangier arrangements.
albums.lineage: Part of the LA singer-songwriter circle overlapping several C6/C5 field-guide artists, working the same funny-sad songwriting vein as the Drag City deadpan school.

albums.label: Earth Libraries
albums.description: Streetsweeper is a tranquil, piano-and-guitar record from Andrews' long-running Yawns project. It's quieter and more contemplative than his fuller band records, closer to Little Wings' loose, handmade songwriting, for listeners who like soft-spoken, homespun songs.
albums.lineage: The latest entry in Andrews' long-running solo project, which sounds close to Little Wings' loose DIY songwriting.

albums.label: Dead Oceans
albums.description: Morby's latest album works in a bucolic folk-rock palette, continuing the warm, unhurried style of This Is a Photograph with an even more pastoral, near-spiritual tone. Pedal steel and acoustic textures dominate over the breezy tempos. It suits listeners who want gentle, open-hearted songwriting.
albums.lineage: Extends Morby's Dead Oceans-era folk-rock songwriting, which sounds indebted to Dylan and cosmic country.

albums.label: Kill Rock Stars
albums.description: A 'canyon country' record that balances light and dark more explicitly than Davis's earlier work while keeping her harp and full-band folk-rock sound intact. Harmonized guitars and road-song imagery push it toward neo-western country rock. It suits listeners who like breezy, anthemic California-style songwriting.
albums.lineage: Continues Davis's arc from harp-led pop toward songwriting that sounds indebted to Laurel Canyon and cosmic country.

albums.label: Truth Zone Records
albums.description: Recorded at Chicago's Thawed Out festival, this live document catches Sam Cantor's band stretching their warm, Dead-adjacent country-rock songs out on stage. Guitars trade lines over an easy groove, for fans who want the band looser than on record.
albums.lineage: A live snapshot of Chicago's small cosmic-country scene, sounding close to the city's guitar-forward underground around acts like Ryley Walker.
key_tracks: I Could See It Coming (Live at Thawed Out)

albums.label: Sacred Bones Records
albums.description: Cogan's Sacred Bones record mixes haunted folk, psych rock and a shadowy strain of country. Pedal steel and mandolin ground the record's smoky, '70s-inflected atmosphere, with her voice hushed and drawling. It suits listeners who like their country dark and dreamlike.
albums.lineage: A shift for Cogan from her earlier dream-folk toward country and psych-rock textures that sound akin to the wider cosmic-country revival.

albums.label: Full Time Hobby
albums.description: The third entry in pedal-steel player Spencer Cullum's Coin Collection series, built around English folklore. Pedal steel and fingerpicked acoustic guitar drift through a kaleidoscopic, hushed mix of folk, jazz and pop. It suits listeners who like pastoral, gently psychedelic folk.
albums.lineage: An English-born Nashville pedal-steel player's solo series, sounding indebted to English folk-rock and pulled into a cosmic-country frame.

albums.label: Rough Trade Records
albums.description: Ballgame's full-length debut sets warm, '70s-inflected songwriting inside commanding, theatrical vocal performances and tasteful, non-pastiche arrangements. It leans closer to Laurel Canyon soft-rock revivalism than jam-band twang, but fits the same '70s-revival umbrella.
albums.lineage: A newer entry in the '70s soft-rock/country-rock revival that runs alongside this lane's jammier, Dead-descended wing.

albums.label: Self-released
albums.description: Way Dynamic continues Dylan Young's painstaking attention to '70s-styled folk-rock harmonies and drum sounds, mixing sincere songwriting with oddball funk detours. Strings and close harmonies keep the mood hushed and breezy.
albums.lineage: Continues Young's Melbourne chamber-pop lineage established on Duck and So Familiar.
